# Flat symmetric rounding removes the free-simplex compatibility hypothesis

Let \(n\ge1,d\ge2\), and let \(P\subset\mathbb Z^n\) be finite,
lattice-complete, centrally symmetric, and affinely spanning
\(\mathbb R^n\). Let \(K_z\subset\mathbb R^d\), \(z\in P\), be
full-dimensional compact convex fibers satisfying all actual anchored
Minkowski inclusions, with
\[
 K_{-z}=-K_z.
\]
Suppose \(K_p\) is a simplex at some \(p\ne0\). Write
\(M=\sum_z|K_z|>0\), \(D=M/2\).

After a fixed allowed linear shear, choose the canonical \(d+1\) cap
group determined by the centered simplex at \(p\), as defined below.
Then in EVERY neighborhood of this finite fiber family and this cap
group there is an actual compatible family, with the same positive
integer support \(P\), and a nearby whole-space-covering group such that
\[
 M_{\rm new}>M,\qquad
 \mu_{\rm new}(H_i^{\rm new})<D\quad(0\le i\le d).               \tag{1}
\]
Only the selected group is constrained. Other original cap budgets are
not asserted preserved.

In particular the open free-fiber compatibility assumption in Section 6
of candidate 30d7d56bee7b8657 can be removed
by an EXACTLY cap-budget-flat preliminary perturbation. Arbitrary other
fibers need not have differentiable cap functions. The proof does not
invoke a generic smoothing principle or assert that adding a ball
removes flat faces.

## 1. Coordinates, the selected cover, and baseline flatness

Choose a real base functional \(v\) with \(v\cdot p=1\), and let \(c\)
be the centroid of \(K_p\). The fixed shear
\[
 (z,x)\mapsto(z,x-c(v\cdot z))
\]
centers the simplex and its reflected mate, preserves every integer
base and continuous fiber volume, and commutes with central reflection.
Work in these coordinates and call the selected centered simplex \(K\),
of volume \(V\). Put \(m=d+1\), \(\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d\), and write its
barycentric coordinates as
\[
 \lambda_i(x)=l_i(x)+1/m,\qquad \sum_i l_i=0.
\]
For \(a\) near \(a^*=m^{-1}{\bf1}\), with \(\sum_i a_i=1\), define
\[
 H_i(a)=\{l_i(x)-(a_i-1/m)(v\cdot z)\ge0\}.                      \tag{2}
\]
At \(p\) this is \(\lambda_i(x)\ge a_i\). The margins sum to zero,
so the group covers ALL \(\mathbb R^{n+d}\), not only the source.

Every cap in (2) passes through the global symmetry center and has a
nonzero continuous normal. Its boundary is null in every full-dimensional
fiber. Reflection therefore makes its mass exactly \(D\) on the original
source for EVERY nearby \(a\). This is a statement about the sum over
all fibers; individual other-fiber cap masses need not be smooth.

## 2. Flat strictification and an actual open neighborhood

Choose \(R>\max_{z\in P}|z|^2\), let
\(\phi_z=R-|z|^2>0\), and let \(B\) be the Euclidean unit ball. Put
\[
 \widehat K_z^\epsilon=K_z+\epsilon\phi_zB,\quad
 \widehat M_\epsilon=\sum_z|\widehat K_z^\epsilon|,\quad
 \alpha_\epsilon=(M/\widehat M_\epsilon)^{1/d},\quad
 L_z^\epsilon=\alpha_\epsilon\widehat K_z^\epsilon.             \tag{3}
\]
These families remain centrally symmetric, their total mass is exactly
\(M\), and every nonvertical through-origin cap has mass exactly \(D\).
In particular the original canonical group \(H_i(a^*)\) has exactly
its old budgets. Hausdorff convergence and full-dimensionality give
\(\widehat M_\epsilon\to M\), so \(\alpha_\epsilon\to1\).

Here is the precise uniform compatibility margin. For a representation
\(z=\sum_w\theta_w w\) with \(\theta_z=0\), and every unit continuous
normal \(u\),
\[
 h_{\widehat K_z^\epsilon}(u)
  -\sum_w\theta_wh_{\widehat K_w^\epsilon}(u)
 \ge\epsilon\sum_w\theta_w|w-z|^2
 \ge\epsilon\Delta_P^2,                                      \tag{4}
\]
where \(\Delta_P=\min_{w\ne z}|w-z|>0\).
Representations with \(0<\theta_z<1\) reduce to these after removing
the selfweight and renormalizing; \(\theta_z=1\) is the identity.

Consequently any independently perturbed compact convex fibers
\(J_z\), within Hausdorff distance
\(\epsilon\Delta_P^2/4\) of \(\widehat K_z^\epsilon\), still satisfy
all anchored inclusions, strictly for excluded-self representations.
Indeed a support gap changes by at most twice that distance.
The analogous normalized radius is
\(\alpha_\epsilon\epsilon\Delta_P^2/4\).
There are only finitely many source fibers but the estimate covers ALL
real coefficients in every anchored representation.

The convex hull of the lifted perturbed fibers has exactly those fibers
at every \(z\in P\), by the inclusions, and no other integer bases because
\(\operatorname{conv}P\cap\mathbb Z^n=P\).
The positive fibers and the full base span make this hull
full-dimensional. Thus (4) is an actual open feasibility neighborhood,
not merely formal slack in a finite sample of inequalities.

## 3. A face-tube regularity lemma for the selected simplex

Let \(Q(W)\) be a labeled affine perturbation of the fixed simplex \(K\);
its barycentric vertex matrix \(W\) has column sums one and is near \(I\).
Let a cap \(u\cdot x\ge b\) have exactly one positive vertex, say \(i\),
and all other vertex values negative, with a fixed nonzero margin.
Canonical caps and all sufficiently nearby proper caps have this property.

For sufficiently small \(\tau\ge0\), the functions
\[
 |Q(W)+\tau B|,\qquad
 |(Q(W)+\tau B)\cap\{u\cdot x\ge b\}|                          \tag{5}
\]
are finite polynomials in \(\tau\) of degree at most \(d\), whose
coefficients are smooth in \(W,u,b\) on one common neighborhood.
In particular they and all their parameter derivatives through order
two converge uniformly on a smaller compact neighborhood to their
\(\tau=0\) counterparts, with error \(O(\tau)\).
This lemma permits moving proper cap normals as well as thresholds.

We give the geometric proof, including the source of this regularity.
Write \(Q(W)=A_WK+t_W\), where \(A_W\) is invertible near \(I\).
Each point of a convex parallel body has a unique nearest point in
the original polytope. If that nearest point is in the relative
interior of a face \(F(W)\), the displacement lies in its normal cone.
Up to null boundaries this partitions \(Q(W)+\tau B\) into orthogonal
face tubes
\[
 F(W)+\bigl(N_{Q(W)}(F(W))\cap\tau B\bigr).                     \tag{6}
\]
For a \(k\)-face, product measure is its \(k\)-area times Lebesgue
measure in its \((d-k)\)-dimensional normal space.

A face not containing vertex \(i\) lies uniformly on the negative side
of the cap, so its entire small tube contributes zero.
For a face containing \(i\), put
\(h_j=u\cdot v_j(W)-b\). A fixed displacement \(w\) changes all these
heights by \(u\cdot w\). The sign pattern remains one positive vertex.
For \(k\ge1\) the exact retained \(k\)-area is
\[
 |F(W)|_k\,
 \frac{(h_i+u\cdot w)^k}
      {\prod_{j\in\operatorname{vert}F,\ j\ne i}
              u\cdot(v_i(W)-v_j(W))}.                       \tag{7}
\]
All denominators are uniformly positive. For \(k=0\), the selected
vertex contributes its full normal-sector volume. The full face
\(k=d\) gives the usual unrounded simplex cap.

To put the remaining normal integrations on fixed domains, let
\(E_F\) be the normal space of the reference face and let
\(\Theta_F=N_K(F)\cap S(E_F)\). The transformed normal cone is exactly
\(A_W^{-T}N_K(F)\). Write \(L_W=A_W^{-T}|_{E_F}\), let \(J_W\) be its
subspace Jacobian, and set \(q=d-k\ge1\). Polar coordinates on the
reference cone give
\[
 w=\tau r\,\frac{L_W\theta}{|L_W\theta|},\quad
 dw=J_W\tau^q |L_W\theta|^{-q}r^{q-1}\,dr\,d\sigma(\theta),
 \qquad0\le r\le1,\quad\theta\in\Theta_F.                     \tag{8}
\]
The fixed spherical cone has finite measure. The factors involving
\(L_W,J_W\) and all their derivatives are uniformly bounded, since
\(A_W\) remains invertible. Substitute (8) into (7) and expand its
degree-\(k\) numerator: each tube is \(\tau^q\) times a polynomial of
degree at most \(k\) in \(\tau\), with smooth coefficients.
Differentiation under these fixed finite integrals is justified by
the displayed uniform bounds. The same argument without the indicator
proves the volume assertion in (5). Summing the finitely many faces
proves the lemma.

The coefficient formula even provides a smooth algebraic extension to
negative \(\tau\), although no negative-radius body is asserted.
Thus ordinary parameter versions of the implicit function theorem
can be applied at \(\tau=0\). The proof never requires smooth boundary
curvature of \(Q(W)+\tau B\), which still has flat faces.

## 4. Global cap increments use only this regular selected fiber

For now work before the common normalization in (3). Fix \(\epsilon>0\)
and put \(\tau=\epsilon\phi_p\). Vary only the selected fiber by
\[
 \widehat K_p^\epsilon(W)=Q(W)+\tau B,
\]
keeping every other \(\widehat K_z^\epsilon\) fixed.
Define
\[
\begin{split}
 V_\epsilon(W)&=|Q(W)+\tau B|-|K+\tau B|,\\
 F_{\epsilon i}(W,a)&=
 |(Q(W)+\tau B)\cap\{\lambda_i(x)\ge a_i\}|,\\
 C_{\epsilon i}(W,a)&=
 F_{\epsilon i}(W,a)-F_{\epsilon i}(I,a).
\end{split}                                                   \tag{9}
\]
On the entire unchanged symmetric family, every cap \(H_i(a)\) has
mass \(\widehat M_\epsilon/2\) identically in \(a\). Therefore its
EXACT global cap mass after the single-fiber change is
\[
 \widehat\mu_{\epsilon,W}(H_i(a))
   =\widehat M_\epsilon/2+C_{\epsilon i}(W,a).                \tag{10}
\]
No regularity of the separate cap contributions of other fibers is
needed. Their total baseline contribution has been canceled exactly.
In particular \(C_{\epsilon i}(I,a)=0\) identically, including all
pure threshold derivatives.

The face-tube lemma says that \(V_\epsilon,C_\epsilon\) converge in
\(C^2\) on a common parameter neighborhood to the original physical
simplex objective and cap increments. Their derivative with respect
to physical \(W\) is onto \(\mathbb R^m\) at \(\epsilon=0\), hence
remains onto for every sufficiently small \(\epsilon\).

## 5. Exact cap equalities and persistent reduced second variation

We use the independently verified algebra in
canonical-selected-star-has-quadratic-joint-escape.md.
At the unrounded point \((I,a^*)\), its normalized cap derivatives are
\[
 f_i(B)=\Gamma\bigl(\operatorname{tr}B+\sum_jB_{ij}\bigr).
\]
There is a fixed physical right inverse \(S\) of this normalized map:
for \(f\in\mathbb R^m\), let \(z_i=f_i/(m\Gamma)\), \(Z=\sum_i z_i\),
and set \(S(f)_{ii}=z_i\), \(S(f)_{ij}=z_i-Z/d\) for \(i\ne j\).
To obtain a right inverse for absolute cap derivatives, put
\(\mathcal Rf=S(f/V)\).

That note constructs a physical velocity \(B_0\) and threshold velocity
\(\omega=e_1-e_0\), with
\[
 \operatorname{tr}B_0=0,\quad f(B_0)=0,\quad
 Q=\frac{d-1}{d}\left(2-\frac1{d+1}\right)>0,                  \tag{11}
\]
such that the Hessian of
\[
 V_0(W)-\frac1{m\Gamma}\sum_i C_{0i}(W,a)
\]
on \((B_0,\omega)\) is \(VQ\). The full first derivative of this
Lagrangian vanishes. All these are exact physical simplex identities.

Set
\[
 W(t,r)=I+tB_0+\mathcal Rr,\qquad a(t)=a^*+t\omega.
\]
The Jacobian with respect to \(r\) of
\(C_\epsilon(W(t,r),a(t))\), at \(t=r=\epsilon=0\), is the identity.
The face-tube lemma and the implicit function theorem yield a unique
smooth local correction \(r=r(t,\epsilon)\), with
\[
 r(0,\epsilon)=0,\qquad
 C_\epsilon(W(t,r(t,\epsilon)),a(t))=0.                       \tag{12}
\]
The zero-\(\epsilon\) first derivative is \(r_t(0,0)=0\).
Let
\[
 J_\epsilon(t)=V_\epsilon(W(t,r(t,\epsilon))).
\]
Then \(J_\epsilon(0)=0\). Differentiating the exact cap equalities at
\(\epsilon=0\), and using the objective-one multipliers
\(1/(m\Gamma)\), gives
\[
 J_0''(0)=VQ>0.                                             \tag{13}
\]
Indeed the correction acceleration cancels the cap second derivatives,
so the reduced objective Hessian equals precisely the Lagrangian
Hessian in (11). Uniform \(C^2\) convergence and the invertible
\(r\)-Jacobian imply \(J_\epsilon''(0)>0\) for all sufficiently small
positive \(\epsilon\).

No stationarity of the rounded family is assumed. Its first derivative
\(J_\epsilon'(0)\) may be nonzero. Nevertheless, for every fixed such
\(\epsilon\) and every sufficiently small \(t>0\),
\[
 J_\epsilon(t)+J_\epsilon(-t)>2J_\epsilon(0)=0.
\]
One sign therefore yields strictly positive volume gain with EVERY
selected cap EXACTLY at its old budget. The parameter \(t\) may be
chosen arbitrarily small, in particular small enough that the moving
rounded fiber remains inside the actual compatibility neighborhood (4).
This order of choices is important: one does not try to make
\(\epsilon=o(t^2)\) while requiring a physical displacement smaller
than the \(O(\epsilon)\) compatibility slack.

At the chosen nearby point the physical cap Jacobian is still onto.
Apply the same implicit correction with cap target vector
\(-\eta{\bf1}\), for a sufficiently small \(\eta>0\).
Continuity preserves the already strict volume gain and the open
compatibility neighborhood, while every selected global cap is now
strictly below its baseline budget. This proves a genuine all-cap
improvement, not merely an improvement of a multiplier-weighted sum.

Finally apply the fixed common dilation \(\alpha_\epsilon\) from (3)
to this perturbed family and all its cap planes. Every mass is multiplied
by \(\alpha_\epsilon^d\). The unchanged baseline total becomes \(M\),
the baseline cap budget becomes \(D\), and the strict inequalities
become exactly (1). The normalized cap group can be written
\[
 l_i(x)-\alpha_\epsilon(a_i-1/m)(v\cdot z)\ge0;
\]
its margins still sum to zero. All members remain nonvertical.
Taking \(\epsilon\) and then the physical displacement arbitrarily small
proves the claimed neighborhood statement.

## 6. Boundary, support, and dimensional scope

If starting from a compact centrally symmetric convex body that has
additional zero-\(d\)-volume integer fibers, first retain its positive
indices \(P\) and take the hull of their fibers. The set \(P\) is
lattice-complete: every integer convex combination of positive fibers
contains a positive-volume Minkowski combination in the original body.
It is symmetric, and the retained hull preserves the entire original
mixed measure and every positive fiber. The theorem concerns this
finite-fiber geometry; it makes no unsupported assertion that omitted
real-base portions of a larger original body are Hausdorff-close.

If \(P\) has affine rank \(k<n\), symmetry makes its affine hull linear.
Use the saturated lattice \( \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}P\cap
\mathbb Z^n\) and a unimodular coordinate change to put it in
\(\mathbb R^k\times\{0\}\). The argument applies there unchanged.
If a full-dimensional body in the original ambient space is desired,
take the resulting hull times a centered base cube of side less than
one in the missing integer directions. Only transverse integer
coordinate zero occurs, so every positive integer fiber and cap mass
is exactly preserved. Extend \(v\) by zero in those coordinates.
This is an explicit completion of the retained source, not a claim
about convergence to arbitrary omitted real-base geometry.

The case \(d=1\) is excluded because the positive joint Hessian (11)
vanishes. No statement is made for non-simplex selected fibers or
for a class constraining the number of physical facets.

The original centrally symmetric source has exact maximum absolute
depth \(M/2\): its symmetry center is actual and every closed through-cap
has at least half the mass, while opposite nonvertical caps at any
candidate sum to \(M\). The new group covers every point and has each
cap strictly smaller than \(M/2\), while total mass has increased.
This is a selected-cover variation result on an already OC-safe source,
not a general OC conclusion.

The companion verifier is
verify_flat_symmetric_rounding_joint_escape.py.

## 7. Independent planar formula and an initially active model

For a triangle \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(v_0,v_1,v_2)\) and a proper
one-positive-vertex cap at \(i\), set
\[
 h_i=u\cdot v_i-b>0,\quad D_{ij}=u\cdot(v_i-v_j)>0,
\]
and let \(L_{ij}\), \(n_{ij}\) be the length and outward unit normal
of its adjacent edge, and \(\theta_i\) its exterior angle.
The face tubes give the exact local formula
\[
\begin{split}
 |(Q+\tau B)\cap H|
  ={}&|Q\cap H|
   +\tau\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{L_{ij}h_i}{D_{ij}}\\
   &+\frac{\tau^2}{2}\left[
      \theta_i+\sum_{j\ne i}
                    \frac{L_{ij}(u\cdot n_{ij})}{D_{ij}}
                    \right].                              \tag{20}
\end{split}
\]
The selected vertex sector is fully inside the cap; other vertex
sectors are outside. Each adjacent edge strip integrates the retained
edge length \(L_{ij}(h_i+s\,u\cdot n_{ij})/D_{ij}\) over
\(0\le s\le\tau\). This independently verifies every term and sign
in (20). Total area is
\(|Q|+\tau\,\operatorname{perimeter}Q+\pi\tau^2\).

For a concrete active-compatibility source, take the centered standard
triangle \(K=T-(1/3,1/3)\) and fibers
\[
 -K,\qquad (K-K)/2,\qquad K
\]
at bases \(-1,0,1\). The midpoint inclusion is initially an EQUALITY,
so the old free-fiber theorem does not apply. Use
\(\phi=(1,2,1)\). The new midpoint inclusion has ball slack
\(\epsilon B\), and any selected-vertex displacement below \(2\epsilon\)
preserves it. The original mass is \(7/4\); since both \(K\) and
\((K-K)/2\) have perimeter \(2+\sqrt2\), the rounded mass is exactly
\[
 \widehat M_\epsilon=\frac74+4(2+\sqrt2)\epsilon+6\pi\epsilon^2.
                                                               \tag{21}
\]
The verifier implements (20), checks the exact unrounded critical
algebra and reduced curvature \(VQ=5/12\), and performs an independent
high-precision implicit correction for this initially active model.
Its finite numerical tests are supplemental; the general existence
result follows from Sections 2--5.
